root_idea.summary: The root is oriented around softness, ease, and diminished substance or nourishment, with related ideas of readiness and a broken or yielding condition.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence connects this orientation with dyed wool, with something present and readily available, and with a branch bent or broken without separating. Other branches extend these ideas to laxity, poverty, unguarded speech, and specialized natural objects.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under the normalized citation form عِهْنٌ.

senses.definition: Dyed or coloured wool; a tuft or portion of wool.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic simile كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ, it denotes wool, with the lexical discussion especially emphasizing its colour or dye. The supplied Quran contexts render the expression as “like wool.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, dwell, or abide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِالمكانِ, “in the place.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go forth or proceed; of good, to emerge from someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explicitly contrasting use of the verb’s sense of remaining; attested in the construction عَهَنَ مِنْهُ خَيْرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue, last, or endure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a thing that persists or remains in existence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become present or ready.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equivalent in this use to حَضَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, labour, exert oneself, or be diligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested with فِي العَمَلِ, “in the work.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enjoin, charge, or bid someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Given as an equivalent of عَهِدَ; the cited construction is described with إِلَيْهِ following.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten to someone what he wishes or desires.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with لَهُ and the desired object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of palm branches, to become dry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported use concerning palm branches; its analysis is disputed in the wider lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a branch, rod, or twig, to bend or break without becoming detached.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may appear intact but bends when shaken because the break has not produced separation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good manager or tender of property, camels, or cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic description of a person’s care or management of property or livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bending of a branch, rod, or twig, or its breaking without separation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object appears whole but bends when shaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert tree or plant with a red flower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use; the plant is also described as a kind of herb or legume.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rancour, malice, malevolence, spite, or anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal variant of إِحْنَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The base or lower part of a palm-tree raceme.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized palm-botanical term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding; continuing or lasting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active-participial form corresponding to the verb’s persistence-related uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Going forth or proceeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrasting active-participial use opposite to remaining or staying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Present or ready.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to food, beverage, property, camels, or cattle when these are available or at hand.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of property, camels, or cattle, long-possessed, homeborn, or inherited from parents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes established possessions or livestock rather than newly acquired property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a branch, rod, or twig, broken without becoming detached and therefore left suspended and lax.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The branch remains attached despite the break.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lax, sluggish, or lazy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from the condition of a broken, yielding branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poor or reduced in condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use explained through the image of being broken or weakened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The palm branches near the heart or central growth of the palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Regional terminology varies concerning which branches are called عَوَاهِنُ; the term is plural in this use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The limbs or members of a human being used for work or earning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use based on the functional relation of palm branches to the tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Certain veins in a she-camel’s womb or vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use, compared with the branches of a palm tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To utter or cast out speech without thought, caution, or verification.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom may describe speaking without guidance, caring little whether one is right or wrong, or stating what conjecture suggests without certainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A good, pleasant, or sweet plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical term.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Remaining or dwelling in a place.
Contrasting sense of going forth or good emerging.
Hastening a desired thing to someone.
A branch bending or breaking without separation.
Wool, especially dyed or coloured wool, including a tuft or portion.
Idiomatic good management of property or livestock.
The noun for a bent or incompletely broken branch.
Active participle meaning remaining or dwelling.
Contrasting active-participial sense of going forth.
Continuing or lasting is grouped with the persistence-related active-participial sense.
Long-possessed or inherited property and livestock.
Palm branches near the tree’s heart.
Human limbs used for work or earning.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the preceding entry.

cautions: The verb and active participle include explicitly contrasting uses: remaining or continuing versus going forth; these senses should be distinguished by context.

The reported use عَهَنَتْ عَوَاهِنُ النَّخْلِ for palm branches becoming dry is recorded as a lexical sense, but the root discussion disputes that analysis and favors a palm-branch term connected with softness or freshness.
